finding_key: docker-compose.yaml::nothing in the repo registers the yorkie project event webhook, so every environment that isn't manually reconfigured silently loses "last modified"
evidence: The core factual claim holds: `attachMeta` (document.controller.ts) now reads `updatedAt` solely from Postgres, and only the webhook at yorkie-event.controller.ts:38 advances it for content edits, while the only Yorkie deployment artifact supplied (docker-compose.yaml) registers no event webhook — the diff explicitly defers registration to an unchecked manual ops task in docs/tasks/active/20260710-docs-list-updatedat-webhook-todo.md and prose in docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:69. The claim overstates impact, though: `YorkieAdminService.getSummaries` already returned an empty map when `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` is unset and the e2e lane stubs the service, so local dev and the integration lane showed `createdAt` before this change too; the real regression is confined to configured clusters, where the design doc reports the admin read was timing out on ~every poll anyway. I could not check the whole repo for a helm chart or CI step (no checkout mounted), so the "nothing anywhere registers it" part rests on the supplied directory listings and the project's own unchecked ops item.
